description:
List what the authenticated user follows on Zindies — their own
favorites only: creators, creations (ZINEs), places (shops), events, and
the event lists / new-arrivals list they follow — most recently followed
first. Use it for "what am I following?" or "which shops did I save?",
and to learn whether something is already followed before calling
toggle_favorite (which flips the state). It never returns other
people's follows or how many people follow something.

To change a follow use toggle_favorite. For the catalog of every list
that can be followed, with coverage between lists, use
list_followable_zones. For events the user said they will attend use
list_my_participations. Public data (search, list_events, get_*) needs
no token.

Requires a Bearer token (a User API token, or an OAuth token with the
favorites:read scope). Without one the server answers HTTP 401
("unauthorized"), and with a token lacking the scope HTTP 403
("insufficient_scope"); both carry a WWW-Authenticate header that
starts the OAuth sign-in.

Returns `favorites`, `count` (entries in this response) and `has_more`.
Each entry has `type`, `followed_at`, `url` and the same summary fields
as a search hit: `id`, `token`, `name`, `title` for a creator; `id`,
`token`, `title`, `released_year` for a creation; `id`, `token`,
`name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `area` for a place; `id`,
`event_type`, `title`, `kind`, `area` and its dates for an event;
`id`, `slug`, `name`, `kind`, `area` for a list. Pass `token` to
get_creator / get_creation / get_place and an event's `id` to
get_event. To unfollow, pass `type` as target_type to toggle_favorite
with the `token` (an event's `id` as a string, a list's `slug`).

Nothing followed returns `favorites: []`, not an error. Entries that
are no longer public (made private, or an event whose announcement
date was moved to the future) are left out.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return. When `has_more` is true, call again with `offset` raised by this many.

locale.description: Response language for translatable text fields (names, titles, descriptions): ja = Japanese, en = English, ko = Korean, zh-TW = Traditional Chinese. Pass the language the user is conversing in when it is one of these; otherwise omit it. Fields without a translation fall back to their source language (usually Japanese), so one response can mix languages. Tokens, ids, dates and URLs are the same in every locale. Default: ja.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip from the most recently followed, for the next page: 0 (default) for the first page, then `offset` + `limit` while `has_more` is true.

type.description: Return only follows of this kind: `creator`, `creation` (ZINEs and other works), `place` (shops / venues), `event`, `event_zone` (event lists such as "every event in Kanto") or `creation_zone` (the new-arrivals list). The values are those of toggle_favorite's `target_type`. Omit for every kind mixed in one list.

name: list_my_favorites
title: List what you follow
